raw_response:
I am getting older now, so I do not want to make big changes. On my 14 mu, I will still do wheat and maize one after the other, same as most people here. This is the safest way for my family. Wheat gives steady grain, and maize after wheat makes full use of the land. I only finished primary school, so I do not count things too finely. I look at what worked before, what the neighbors are doing, and how much cash I can spare. Fertilizer is expensive, and pumping well water also costs money, but if I cut too much and the crop turns weak, that loss is worse. So this year I will use a moderate amount, not the highest, not too little. For wheat, I will put most fertilizer before sowing, then add some at jointing if the leaves are not dark enough. I will water wheat about three times if the weather is normal. After wheat harvest, I will rush to plant maize quickly, with simple rotary tillage, because the time gap is very short. For maize I will use hybrid seed like other households nearby, put base fertilizer first, then topdress once around knee-high stage. If summer rain is decent, I may only irrigate once, but if it stays dry, I will add one more. I will watch weeds and insects when they come; I do not spray for no reason.
